newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-HUBER MOVES STEP CLOSER TO AUSTRALIAN OPEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HUBER MOVES STEP CLOSER TO AUSTRALIAN OPEN FINAL.

text.p: Fifth seed Anke Huber became the first player through to the final 16 of the Australian Open on Friday, sweeping past Natasha Zvereva in straight sets to move a step closer to her second successive final at Melbourne Park.
Huber, ranked seven in the world but so often playing in the shadow of her top seeded German compatriot Steffi Graf, took just 65 minutes to dispose of Zvereva of Belarus 7-5 6-0.

Huber, who lost the first set in both her earlier matches and has been distracted by the mysterious collapse of her mother on Wednesday, made another slow start on centre court on Friday morning, surrendering her first service game.
But Zvereva, who has made her name by winning 15 doubles grand slam titles, soon ran out of steam just as Huber found her rhythm.
With the match evenly poised at 5-5 in the first set, Huber, who lost to Monica Selea in Melbourne last year, took complete control and raced away by winning eight straight games.
Huber's mother, Gerda, was taken to hospital on Wednesday afternoon after collapsing outside the players' lounge at Melbourne Park. She was given a clean bill of health and discharged.
